summary: This component provides a button that fetches a Markdown version of a blog post and copies it to the clipboard, plus a link to view the raw file. It manages loading, success, and error states, automatically resetting back to idle after two seconds so the user sees visual feedback before the button returns to normal.

explanations.10: This defines the four possible states the copy operation can be in: idle (ready), copying (in progress), copied (success), or error (failed).
explanations.27: We construct the URL to the Markdown file by taking the post's permalink, removing any trailing slash, and appending `.md` — so `/blog/my-post/` becomes `/blog/my-post.md`.
explanations.29: useCallback memoizes this function so it only gets recreated when mdUrl changes, preventing unnecessary re-renders of child components that might receive it as a prop.
explanations.32: We fetch the Markdown file from the server using the constructed URL.
explanations.33: If the HTTP response isn't successful (like a 404), we throw an error so it gets caught by the catch block below.
explanations.35: navigator.clipboard.writeText is the browser API that actually copies text to the user's clipboard.
explanations.44: We only want to auto-reset the status if it's showing success or error feedback; if it's idle or copying, we skip the cleanup timer entirely.
explanations.45: This timer resets the status back to idle after 2 seconds, so the button message returns to the default after showing 'Copied' or 'Could not copy'.
explanations.46: We return a cleanup function that cancels the timer if the component unmounts or status changes before the 2 seconds elapse, preventing memory leaks.
explanations.55: The button is disabled while copying is in progress so the user can't accidentally trigger multiple simultaneous copy attempts.
